research_question: How accurately can a computer-vision model identify common fruit diseases and pests from user-submitted images under real-world lighting and background conditions?
scope_note: Start with 4 fruits and 2–4 conditions each. A smaller, well-evaluated set is stronger research than 100 poorly documented classes.

classes.label: Apple scab
classes.summary: Fungal disease (Venturia inaequalis) that produces olive-brown, velvety spots on leaves and fruit. Lesions may crack or distort fruit surfaces.

classes.label: Apple black rot
classes.summary: Fungal disease (Botryosphaeria obtusa) associated with leaf “frog-eye” spots and rotting fruit with concentric rings.
look_for: Circular leaf spots with purple margins

classes.label: Cedar apple rust
classes.summary: Fungal disease that alternates between apple and juniper/cedar hosts. Bright orange-yellow spots appear on apple leaves.
look_for: Small fruiting structures on the underside

classes.label: Apple — healthy
classes.summary: No disease signs in the image. Healthy apple leaves are typically uniform green without discrete lesions or rust-colored spots.
look_for: No scab, rust, or rot patterns

classes.label: Grape black rot
classes.summary: Fungal disease (Guignardia bidwellii) causing reddish-brown leaf spots and shriveled, mummified berries.
look_for: Hard, black fruit mummies on clusters

classes.label: Grape esca (black measles)
classes.summary: A complex trunk disease. Leaves show tiger-stripe patterns: yellow or red bands between veins, often with necrotic patches.

classes.label: Grape leaf blight
classes.summary: Foliar fungal spotting (often associated with Isariopsis / Pseudocercospora). Angular to irregular dark spots can coalesce.

classes.label: Grape — healthy
classes.summary: No disease signs in the image. Healthy grape leaves are typically broad, lobed, and evenly colored.

classes.label: Peach bacterial spot
classes.summary: Bacterial disease (Xanthomonas) causing small angular leaf spots that may fall out, plus pitted or scabby fruit lesions.

classes.label: Peach — healthy
classes.summary: No disease signs in the image. Healthy peach leaves are typically lance-shaped and evenly green.
look_for: Smooth fruit skin if fruit is visible

classes.label: Tomato early blight
classes.summary: Fungal disease (Alternaria) with target-like concentric rings on older leaves, often starting from the lower canopy.

classes.label: Tomato late blight
classes.summary: Oomycete disease (Phytophthora infestans). Large, water-soaked or greasy lesions can expand rapidly in cool, wet weather.
look_for: White fuzz on undersides in humid conditions

classes.label: Tomato leaf mold
classes.summary: Fungal disease (Passalora fulva) common in humid greenhouses. Pale spots on the upper leaf surface with olive mold beneath.

classes.label: Tomato — healthy
classes.summary: No disease signs in the image. Healthy tomato leaflets are typically deep green without target spots or greasy blotches.
